formation.name: Formation
formation.asks: How hard is it to open and keep open a Christian school?

anchors.4: No registration, approval, or licensure is required to operate. The school notifies the state or does not.
anchors.3: Registration or annual reporting is required and is ministerial: the state records the filing and does not evaluate it.
anchors.2: Approval or accreditation is required, and a religious accreditor recognized by the state satisfies it.
anchors.1: Approval is required and only a state-designated or secular accreditor satisfies it.
anchors.0: Operation without state approval is prohibited, and approval may be withheld on grounds that reach the school's religious character.

autonomy.name: Autonomy
autonomy.asks: How much of the school's own life does the state direct?

anchors.4: Curriculum, texts, calendar, testing, and staffing are the school's own. No state test is mandated.
anchors.3: Broad subject areas are prescribed; content, texts, and staffing are the school's own.
anchors.2: A state assessment is mandated or teacher credentials are required, but the religious content of instruction is not reached.
anchors.1: Curriculum content is prescribed in areas that engage the school's religious teaching, or hiring is constrained in ways that reach religious criteria.
anchors.0: The state prescribes instruction that the school's confession contradicts, with no religious exemption.

portability.name: Portability
portability.asks: Can public funds follow a child to a Christian school, and on what conditions?

anchors.4: A universal program is in force and open to religious schools with no condition that reaches their religious character.
anchors.3: A broad program is in force, income- or category-limited, open to religious schools on the same terms as others.
anchors.2: A narrow program is in force — a tax credit, a small scholarship, or a program limited to particular students.
anchors.1: A program exists in statute but is unfunded, enjoined, or carries conditions that reach religious character.
anchors.0: No program, or religious schools are excluded from every program that exists.

household.name: Household
household.asks: What latitude does a family have outside a conventional school — homeschooling, hybrids, and university-model?

anchors.4: No notice and no assessment required. Hybrid and part-time arrangements are unregulated.
anchors.3: Notice required; no assessment or portfolio review.
anchors.2: Notice plus an assessment or portfolio review, with the reviewer of the family's choosing.
anchors.1: Approval of a plan is required, or review is by a state official, or hybrid arrangements are restricted.
anchors.0: Homeschooling requires state approval that may be withheld, or is available only through a public school program.

security.name: Security
security.asks: How settled is the position — could it change next session?

anchors.4: Protections are constitutional or long-settled; no live challenge and no restrictive constitutional provision.
anchors.3: Statutory and stable; nothing material has changed in five years and nothing is pending.
anchors.2: Statutory, with active legislation or litigation that could move the position in either direction.
anchors.1: A restrictive constitutional provision is in force, or a live case could remove an existing protection.
anchors.0: A protection has been enjoined, repealed, or reversed within the last two years.

tiers.A: The text of an enacted statute, a signed bill, a regulation, or a published opinion.
tiers.B: An official state agency page, an official bill status record, or a governor's published document.
tiers.C: A published summary by a state or national association.
tiers.D: Reported elsewhere; a primary source has not been located. A component at tier D is recorded and is NOT scored.

ed-mi.title: Michigan State Regulation of Private and Home Schools
ed-mi.note: A federal compilation that names the Michigan Compiled Laws section behind each requirement. The statute sections it names are quoted in each entry and are what a re-coder should read.

scotus.title: Opinions of the Supreme Court of the United States
scotus.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
scotus.note: Decision dates, citations, and vote counts as the Court reports them. A vote count is recorded where a court publishes one.

courts.title: Federal appellate and state supreme court opinions
courts.publisher: The courts, via CourtListener and the Free Law Project
courts.note: Published opinions, with the date the court issued them and the docket number it assigned. A vote is recorded where the court reports one.

pl11921.title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act, Pub. L. 119-21, sec. 70411
pl11921.note: The enacted text creating the Education Freedom Tax Credit at 26 U.S.C. sec. 25F.

bp-federal.title: State participation in the federal K-12 education tax credit program
bp-federal.note: A dated secondary tracker of which states have elected. Every election taken from it is tier C and is to be re-coded from the state's own filing or the Treasury's published list.

press-mi.title: Reporting on Michigan's participation decision
press-mi.note: Contemporaneous reporting. Tier C, and to be replaced by the Governor's own filing or its absence from the Treasury list.

bp-universal.title: States with and without universal school choice programs
bp-universal.note: A secondary inventory. Every score taken from it is tier C and is to be re-coded from the enacting statute before it is published as tier A.

formation.note: Every private school other than a church school registers annually on or before 10 October with the Department of Education and reports statistics on uniform blanks the department furnishes, and the section disclaims any authority to license or regulate a private, nonpublic, or church school. Registration that is recorded and not evaluated is the anchor for 3. A church school as defined in section 16-28-1, meaning one operated as a ministry of a local church or association of churches that takes no state or federal funding, is exempt from even that filing and standing alone would sit at 4.

autonomy.note: No curriculum, textbook, calendar, or assessment requirement is imposed on a private or church school, the high school graduation examination is made available to nonpublic students but is not required, and section 16-1-11 expressly withholds authority to license or regulate. Curriculum, texts, calendar, testing, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 4. Recorded caveat: the federal compilation summarizes section 16-1-11.5 as requiring nonpublic school teachers to meet the same certification requirements as public school teachers; the text of that section instead makes the department's own certification and recertification requirements identical for a person who teaches in either sector, and describes a nonpublic church, parochial, or religious school as one 'that is not subject to state regulation.'

portability.instrument: Act 2024-21 (H.B. 129), CHOOSE Act of 2024, § 4(b); Ala. Code §§ 16-6D-1 et seq. (Alabama Accountability Act of 2013)
portability.note: For the years beginning 1 January 2025 and 1 January 2026 the refundable credit funding an education savings account is available only where family adjusted gross income does not exceed 300 percent of the federal poverty level, and from 1 January 2027 it becomes available to any parent of an eligible student. A broad income-limited program open to religious schools on the same terms as others is the anchor for 3; the position in force on the coding date is the income-limited one. Participating schools expressly include church, parochial, and religious schools, and the act forbids any direction or mandate on instructional content or curriculum and any requirement that a provider alter its creed, practices, admissions policies, or hiring policies. The accreditation requirement on participating schools is a condition on the money and is scored here rather than under formation.

household.note: Home education runs either through a church school, where the parent files enrollment documentation with the local public school superintendent and nothing further is required, or through a private tutor, who must hold a certificate issued by the State Superintendent and file a statement of the children and subjects. The church school route, which is the route Alabama families use, is notice with no assessment and no portfolio review, which is the anchor for 3. The tutor route alone would sit lower, but it is an alternative rather than a condition.

security.instrument: Ala. Const. art. XIV, § 263; Magee v. Boyd, 175 So. 3d 79 (Ala. 2015)
security.note: Section 263 provides that no money raised for the support of the public schools shall be appropriated to or used for the support of any sectarian or denominational school, and it carried into the recompiled Constitution of 2022 without change of text. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1 whatever the statutory position. It is not 0: nothing has been enjoined or repealed, and Magee v. Boyd sustained the 2013 programs against challenge, which narrows the exposure without removing the provision.

formation.note: The department is not authorized to require the licensing of religious or other private schools, and a school qualifies as an exempt school by complying with sections 14.45.100 to 14.45.130, which call for a parent enrollment notice to the superintendent, monthly attendance records, and an annual report by 15 October. Reporting that is recorded rather than evaluated is the anchor for 3. Tier B: the compilation names the sections but the statutes could not be opened, because the legislature's statute service would not return section text and the mirror it directs readers to was unreachable.

autonomy.note: An exempt school must offer academic education comparable to that of the public schools and operate at least 180 days, but teacher certification is required only of non-exempt schools, and the testing obligation at section 14.45.120 is a nationally standardized test in grades four, six, and eight rather than a state assessment. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3; it is not 2 because no state assessment is imposed. Tier B: the instruments were not opened.

portability.instrument: Alaska Stat. §§ 14.03.300, 14.03.310; State, Dep't of Educ. & Early Dev. v. Alexander, No. S-19083, Op. No. 7759 (Alaska Mar. 28, 2025)
portability.note: Alaska has no voucher, account, or tax credit for private school tuition. The one instrument under which public money reaches a family is the correspondence student allotment, and section 14.03.310 permits an allotment to buy only nonsectarian services and materials, which is a condition that reaches religious character on its face. A program in statute carrying such a condition is the anchor for 1. Tier B: the allotment statutes themselves were not opened, and the supreme court expressly declined to decide whether allotment funds may be used for private school tuition, so the question is open.

household.note: A child educated at home by a parent is exempt from compulsory attendance with no registration, notification, approval, testing, or form of any kind, and the certified tutor and private school routes are alternatives rather than conditions. No notice and no assessment is the anchor for 4. Tier B: the instrument was not opened.

security.instrument: Alaska Const. art. VII, § 1; State, Dep't of Educ. & Early Dev. v. Alexander, No. S-19083, Op. No. 7759 (Alaska Mar. 28, 2025)
security.note: Article VII, section 1 provides that no money shall be paid from public funds for the direct benefit of any religious or other private educational institution, and it has never been amended. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1, and a live case points the same way: the supreme court vacated the facial ruling in March 2025 but remanded for an as-applied challenge and left open whether allotments may pay private school tuition.

formation.note: Nothing is required of the school itself: no registration, approval, accreditation, or licensure exists in Arizona law for a private school. The only filing is an affidavit of intent that the parent files once with the county school superintendent within thirty days, naming the child and the school. The school notifies the state or does not, which is the anchor for 4.

autonomy.note: Instruction must cover reading, grammar, mathematics, social studies, and science, and a private school must run for at least the same number of days and hours as a public school, but no teacher certification is required, no textbook or content standard binds the school, and private and home-schooled students are not subject to the statewide assessment. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3; the calendar condition is what keeps it off 4.

portability.note: Since the 2022-2023 school year a qualified student includes any resident eligible to enroll in a public school in the state in a preschool program for children with disabilities, kindergarten, or grades one through twelve. Section 15-2404 provides that the chapter permits no government agency to control or supervise a nonpublic school, that a qualified school need not alter its creed, practices, admissions policy, or curriculum to participate, and that the state bears the burden in any proceeding challenging the chapter's application to a qualified school. Universal eligibility with no condition reaching religious character is the anchor for 4.

household.instrument: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 15-802(A), (B)(2), (C); Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 15-745
household.note: The parent files a notarized affidavit of intent with the county school superintendent within thirty days of beginning, and it is not required again unless instruction stops and resumes. No assessment, portfolio, or review follows, and home-schooled students are not subject to the statewide assessment. Notice with no assessment is the anchor for 3.

security.instrument: Ariz. Const. art. IX, § 10; Ariz. Const. art. II, § 12; Cain v. Horne, 220 Ariz. 77 (2009)
security.note: Article IX, section 10 provides that no tax shall be laid or appropriation of public money made in aid of any church, or private or sectarian school. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1, and this one is not dormant: the supreme court used it in 2009 to strike down two voucher programs, and the account program survives only on the reasoning of a 2013 court of appeals decision that the specified object is the family rather than the school.

formation.note: The federal compilation records no accreditation, registration, licensing, or approval requirement of any kind for an Arkansas private school, the only cited provision being the general incorporation section. Nothing is filed and nothing is approved, which is the anchor for 4. The accreditation requirement at Ark. Code Ann. § 6-18-2507(a)(1) attaches only to a school that takes account money and is scored under portability. Tier B: the instrument was not opened.

autonomy.note: No subject areas are prescribed, no teacher certification is required, no calendar is set, and no state assessment applies. Curriculum, texts, calendar, testing, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 4. Recorded caveat for a later coder: instruction must be given in English under section 6-16-104, on pain of a daily fine, and the flag must be displayed under section 6-16-105(b); a coder who treats a medium-of-instruction rule as a curriculum prescription would land on 3. Tier B: the instruments were not opened.

portability.instrument: Act 237 of 2023 (S.B. 294), Arkansas LEARNS Act, § 42; Ark. Code Ann. §§ 6-18-2503(4), 6-18-2507(a)(3)(C)
portability.note: For the 2025-2026 school year and each year thereafter any resident of the state eligible to enroll in a public elementary or secondary school is eligible, and there is no limitation on participation. Universal eligibility in force is the anchor for 4. A participating private school must be accredited by, an associate member of, or an applicant to the Arkansas Nonpublic School Accrediting Association or another accreditor the state board recognizes, which a religious school satisfies through a religious accreditor, so no condition reaches religious character.

household.note: Written notice goes to the superintendent by 15 August, or by 15 December for the spring semester, describing the basic core curriculum and a proposed schedule of instruction, with a signed waiver acknowledging that the state is not liable. No assessment and no portfolio review follows. Notice with no assessment is the anchor for 3. Tier B: the instruments were not opened.

security.instrument: Arkansas Department of Education v. Faulkenberry, 2025 Ark. 203 (No. CV-24-803); Lara v. Faulkenberry, 2025 Ark. 205 (No. CV-24-754)
security.note: A live case could remove an existing protection. The supreme court dismissed the state's sovereign immunity appeal on 11 December 2025 and remanded the intervention question, and the underlying illegal-exaction claim that the Educational Freedom Account program violates article 14, sections 1 through 3, and article 16, section 11 remains pending in the Pulaski County Circuit Court, seeking to stop tuition payments and recover funds already paid. That is the anchor for 1. Arkansas has no Blaine amendment, which is the only reason it is not lower.

formation.note: Section 33190 requires an annual affidavit filed with the Superintendent of Public Instruction, and section 48222 states that the district's verification of that filing 'shall not be construed as an evaluation, recognition, approval, or endorsement of any private school or course.' Annual reporting that the state records and does not evaluate is the anchor for 3.

autonomy.instrument: Cal. Educ. Code § 48222; Doe v. California Lutheran High School Ass'n, 170 Cal. App. 4th 828 (2009)
autonomy.note: A private school must be taught in English and 'offer instruction in the several branches of study required to be taught in the public schools,' but teaching is by 'persons capable of teaching' with no credential, the state content standards do not bind private schools, and private school students do not take the state assessment. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3.

portability.instrument: Cal. Const. art. IX, § 8; Cal. Const. art. XVI, § 5
portability.note: Article IX, section 8 bars appropriation of public money for the support of any sectarian or denominational school, and article XVI, section 5 bars aid to any school controlled by a religious denomination. No program is in force and Proposition 38 was rejected in 2000. The anchor for no program.

household.instrument: Cal. Educ. Code §§ 33190, 48222; Jonathan L. v. Superior Court, 165 Cal. App. 4th 1074 (2008)
household.note: Home education proceeds under the private school affidavit, which is an annual filing and nothing more: no assessment, portfolio, or review of any kind is required of a family on that route. Notice with no assessment is the anchor for 3. The separate tutor exemption at section 48224 requires a credentialed tutor but is not the route families use.

security.instrument: Cal. Const. art. IX, § 8; Cal. Const. art. XVI, § 5
security.note: Two restrictive constitutional provisions are in force, section 8 adopted in 1879 and section 5 in its present form added by Proposition 8 in 1974. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1 whatever the statutory position.

formation.note: A child is exempt from compulsory attendance by enrolling for at least 172 days in an independent or parochial school that provides a basic academic education. No registration, approval, accreditation, or licensure is required to operate one, and section 22-1-114 asks only for a written statement of names, ages, residences, and days of attendance when the local board requests it, not more than once a month. No registration or approval is the anchor for 4. Recorded caveat: the federal compilation reports a mandatory license from the Secretary of State under C.R.S. 24-48.5-101; nothing in title 22 supports that, and the cited section does not govern K-12 schools.

autonomy.note: The statute prescribes a sequential program that must include the communication skills of reading, writing, and speaking, mathematics, history, civics, literature, and science, and sets a 172-day minimum, but it prescribes no content, no texts, and no staffing, requires no educator license, and section 22-7-1006.3(3)(b) exempts a child enrolled in a nonpublic school from the state assessments. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3.

portability.instrument: Colo. Const. art. IX, § 7; Taxpayers for Public Education v. Douglas County School District, 2015 CO 50, 351 P.3d 461
portability.note: Article IX, section 7 forbids the general assembly or any local public corporation ever to pay anything from any public fund in aid of any church or sectarian society, for any sectarian purpose, or to support any school controlled by a church or sectarian denomination. No scholarship, account, or tax credit program for private school attendance is in force: the 2003 pilot program was struck down in 2004 and the Douglas County program was held to violate section 7 in 2015. The anchor for no program.

household.note: Written notification goes to a school district fourteen days before the program begins and each year after, and the child is evaluated at grades three, five, seven, nine, and eleven by a nationally standardized test or by a qualified person the parent selects, with the result submitted to the district or to an independent or parochial school. The evaluator is the family's own choice, which is the anchor for 2. It is not 1: no plan is approved and the district's role is confined to acting on a stated result, though if a composite score falls at or below the thirteenth percentile the district must require placement in a school until the next testing period.

security.instrument: Colo. Const. art. IX, § 7; Colorado Amendment 80 (2024)
security.note: A restrictive constitutional provision is in force and has been used within the last decade to enjoin a program, which is the anchor for 1. The one route around it was closed by the voters: Amendment 80, which would have written a right to school choice into the constitution, failed in November 2024 at 49.32 percent against a 55 percent threshold. Nothing is currently pending, which is why it is not lower.

formation.note: No registration and no approval is required to operate: state approval of a private school is optional and is sought only by schools that want it, and licensing applies only to a school serving children under five. What remains is the section 10-188 obligation to file attendance reports and reports similar to those required of public schools. Reporting that is recorded rather than evaluated is the anchor for 3. Tier B: the statutes could not be opened, because the General Assembly's statute service failed certificate verification on every attempt.

autonomy.note: Instruction must be in English and must cover United States history and citizenship, and a tax-exempt school must teach government at all levels and the duties, responsibilities, and rights of citizenship, but no teacher certification is required, no calendar is set, and no state assessment applies to private school students. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3. Tier B: the statutes were not opened.

portability.instrument: Conn. Const. art. VII; Connecticut State Department of Education inventory of school choice options
portability.note: The department's own inventory of what school choice means in Connecticut lists agricultural science and technology programs, charter schools, magnet schools, technical high schools, and the Open Choice interdistrict program, every one of them public. No voucher, account, scholarship, or tax credit for attendance at a private school exists, and Connecticut has no anti-aid clause that would bar one. The anchor for no program. Tier B: an official state agency page rather than a statute.

household.note: The statute requires only that a child elsewhere receive equivalent instruction in the studies taught in the public schools. The department's own homeschooling page asks families to give the district notice and describes keeping a portfolio as a best practice, and presents neither as a legal requirement. No notice and no assessment required by law is the anchor for 4. Recorded caveat: the federal compilation states the notice of intent and an annual portfolio review as requirements; the department's page does not, and the statute could not be opened to settle it.

security.instrument: Conn. Public Act 21-6 (Substitute S.B. 568), amending Conn. Gen. Stat. § 10-204a; Conn. Const. art. VII
security.note: Connecticut has no Blaine amendment or anti-aid clause, so no restrictive constitutional provision is in force, and nothing is pending on the register. The last material change was Public Act 21-6, which removed the nonmedical exemption to the school immunization requirement for children attending private school, signed on 28 April 2021 and now more than five years old. Statutory with nothing pending is the anchor for 3; it is not 4 because there is no constitutional protection to rest on, only the absence of a constitutional bar.

formation.note: A student is exempt from compulsory attendance where the private school is subject to and in compliance with section 2704, which requires every person conducting a nonpublic school to report end-of-year attendance to the Department of Education by 31 July and a statement of pupil enrollment by 30 September. There is no accreditation, licensing, or approval to be granted or withheld. Annual reporting that is recorded rather than evaluated is the anchor for 3.

autonomy.note: A private school must give regular and thorough instruction in the subjects prescribed for the public schools in a manner suitable to children of the same age and stage of advancement, and section 4103 adds courses on the United States and Delaware constitutions and the free enterprise system, but licensure and certification of nonpublic educators is voluntary under section 121(b) and no state assessment is imposed. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3.

portability.instrument: Del. Const. art. X, § 3
portability.note: No portion of any fund now existing, or which may hereafter be appropriated or raised by tax for educational purposes, shall be appropriated to, used by, or in aid of any sectarian, church, or denominational school. No voucher, account, scholarship, or tax credit program for private school attendance is in force, and none appears on the register for the period covered. The anchor for no program.

household.note: A homeschool is a nonpublic school for purposes of the attendance chapter, so a single-family or multi-family homeschool reports enrollment and attendance under section 2704 and does nothing else: no curriculum is prescribed to it, no assessment is required, and no review takes place. Notice with no assessment is the anchor for 3. The third form, a single-family homeschool coordinated with the local school district, does require a curriculum approved by the superintendent, but it is one of three options rather than a condition on the others.

security.instrument: Del. Const. art. X, § 3
security.note: A restrictive constitutional provision is in force and has not been amended or repealed during the period covered, which is the anchor for 1 whatever the statutory position. Nothing is pending on the register, which is why it is not lower.

formation.note: The Superintendent must require a school not affiliated with the public system to present evidence satisfactory to the Superintendent that its amount of instruction, character of instruction, staff qualifications, and conditions such as class size and facilities are acceptable to the Board, and approval is contingent on continued submission of attendance records. The safe harbor at section 2100.3 runs only through named regional and independent associations or another accrediting body the Board approves, none of them religious. Approval required, with only a state-designated or secular accreditor satisfying it, is the anchor for 1. It is not 0: nothing in the stated criteria reaches a school's religious character. Recorded caveat: D.C. Code § 38-202(a) was amended in 2013 to substitute 'an educational institution' for the former list of approved schools, and section 38-201(2A) defines that term without an approval qualifier, so a later coder may find the regulation's own premise no longer triggered.

autonomy.note: The Board judges the character of instruction, meaning acceptable subject matter and the time devoted to the subjects, and the training and educational requirements for teaching and supervisory staff must be acceptable to the Board, though a District teaching certificate is not required. A staffing credential requirement, imposed without reaching the religious content of instruction, is the anchor for 2 rather than 3. It is not 1 because nothing in the rule prescribes content that engages a school's religious teaching or constrains hiring on religious criteria.

portability.instrument: Scholarships for Opportunity and Results Act, Pub. L. 112-10, div. C, §§ 3003, 3006; D.C. Code §§ 38-1853.03, 38-1853.06
portability.note: The Opportunity Scholarship Program's stated purpose is to provide low-income parents residing in the District with expanded opportunities, with priority to students from the lowest-performing schools, and the findings state that funds are needed for private educational environments regardless of whether they are secular or nonsecular. A narrow program is the anchor for 2: eligibility is income-limited, the appropriation is fixed and the program has been consistently oversubscribed, and awards are made by lottery, so the great majority of eligible children do not receive one. The certificate of approval regime for nonpublic special education schools under D.C. Law 16-269 is a further condition on District money and belongs here rather than under formation.

household.note: Written notice goes to the state agency fifteen business days before instruction begins and is renewed each August, the parent must hold a high school diploma or a waiver, the program must cover a prescribed list of subjects, and a portfolio must be kept and produced on request. The agency itself decides whether the child is receiving thorough, regular instruction, issues a Notification of Deficiencies, must approve the parent's Corrective Action Plan, and on a Letter of Non-Compliance the parent must enroll the child in a school within forty-five days. Review by a state official is the anchor for 1.

security.instrument: Scholarships for Opportunity and Results Reauthorization Act, Pub. L. 115-31, tit. IX; Pub. L. 111-8, div. C, tit. III
security.note: The District has no restrictive constitutional provision, the program was reauthorized in 2017, and nothing material has changed since and nothing is pending on the register. Statutory with nothing pending is the anchor for 3. It is not 4: the program rests on a federal statute funded by annual appropriation, and an appropriations rider in 2009 once closed it to new admissions, so the position is settled only for as long as Congress leaves it so.

formation.note: Each private school files an annual database survey form with a notarized statement, and paragraph (2)(h) states the legislative intent 'not to regulate, control, approve, or accredit private educational institutions' and that the filing may not be used to imply approval. Annual reporting that is recorded and not evaluated is the anchor for 3.

autonomy.note: The state and the district have no authority to oversee or control the curriculum or academic programs of a private school, no teacher certification is required, no assessment is required, and the statute disclaims any intent to regulate churches, their ministries, or religious instruction. Curriculum, texts, testing, and staffing are the school's own, which is the anchor for 4; a minimum school term under Rule 6A-1.09512, F.A.C. conditions the compulsory attendance exemption but reaches nothing else, and the testing and compliance conditions in Rule 6A-6.03315 apply only to schools that choose to take scholarship students.

portability.note: A parent may receive a Family Empowerment Scholarship if the student is a Florida resident and is eligible to enroll in kindergarten through grade 12 in a public school. Household income sets priority order only, not eligibility, and no condition reaches a school's religious character. Universal eligibility in force is the anchor for 4.

household.note: Notice of intent goes to the district superintendent within 30 days, a portfolio must be kept, and an annual educational evaluation must be filed. The parent selects the method and the evaluator, including a teacher of the parent's own choosing. Notice plus an assessment with the reviewer of the family's choosing is the anchor for 2.

security.instrument: Fla. Const. art. I, s. 3; Bush v. Holmes, 919 So. 2d 392 (Fla. 2006)
security.note: Article I, section 3 bars state revenue being taken from the public treasury directly or indirectly in aid of any church, sect, or religious denomination, and the 2012 ballot measure to delete that language failed. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1; Bush v. Holmes shows the uniformity clause has already been used once to strike down a program.

formation.note: No accreditation, registration, licensing, or approval is required to operate a private school in Georgia. What the statute requires is a report of enrollment to the local superintendent within thirty days of the start of the school year giving the name, age, and residence of each student, monthly notice of admissions and withdrawals, and buildings that meet health and safety standards. Reporting that is recorded rather than evaluated is the anchor for 3. The accreditation condition at O.C.G.A. § 20-2A-1(2)(A) applies only to a school taking scholarship or tax credit students and is scored under portability. Tier B: the statute was not opened.

autonomy.note: The statute sets 180 days of instruction with each day at least four and one-half school hours and requires reading, language arts, mathematics, social studies, and science, but no teacher certification is required and no state assessment is imposed on a private school. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3; the prescribed calendar is what keeps it off 4. Tier B: the statute was not opened.

portability.instrument: 2024 Ga. Laws 457 (S.B. 233), Georgia Promise Scholarship Act; O.C.G.A. §§ 20-2B-21(8), 20-2B-22(a), 20-2B-29
portability.note: A student qualifies only if the parent has been a Georgia resident for a year, the student has been continuously enrolled in a Georgia public school across two enrollment counts, the student resides in the attendance zone of a school on the lowest-performing list, and family income does not exceed 400 percent of the federal poverty level, with the program capped by appropriation. A program limited to particular students is the anchor for 2. A private school is defined to include a sectarian school, so no condition reaches religious character; the accreditation requirement in that definition is a condition on the money. The Special Needs Scholarship and the qualified education expense tax credit are narrow on the same reading.

household.note: A declaration of intent goes to the department within thirty days of starting and by 1 September each year after, the parent must hold at least a high school diploma, prescribed subjects and 180 days of four and one-half hours apply, and the student must take a nationally standardized test at least every three years from the end of grade three, administered in consultation with a person trained in norm-referenced tests, with the records retained by the parent. The department states it has no authority beyond collecting the declaration and may not recommend the test. Notice plus an assessment with the reviewer of the family's choosing is the anchor for 2. Tier B: an official state agency document, not the statute. Recorded caveat: the federal compilation reports no assessment requirement at all, which the department's own document contradicts.

security.instrument: Ga. Const. art. I, § II, para. VII; Gaddy v. Georgia Department of Revenue, No. S17A0177 (Ga. June 26, 2017)
security.note: No money shall ever be taken from the public treasury, directly or indirectly, in aid of any church, sect, cult, or religious denomination or of any sectarian institution. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1 whatever the statutory position, and Georgia's tax credit survived in 2017 only on the ground that the taxpayers lacked standing, so the provision has never been tested on the merits against a choice program. The Promise Scholarship, which pays from the treasury rather than forgiving a tax, is one year old.

formation.instrument: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 302A-1132; Hawaii Council of Private Schools licensing standards
formation.note: The state imposes no education-agency approval, accreditation, or licensure on a private school. Accreditation and licensing are both carried by the Hawaii Council of Private Schools and are optional, and the only mandatory registration is the ordinary business charter and general excise tax licence that any entity in the state obtains from the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs. No education registration or approval is the anchor for 4. Tier B: the compulsory attendance statute could not be opened, because the legislature's statute service refused every request.

autonomy.instrument: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 302A-1132; Hawaii Council of Private Schools licensing standards
autonomy.note: No state curriculum, calendar, staffing, or testing requirement reaches a private school: the compilation records no state testing policy, and the school year length, subject list, staff qualifications, and recordkeeping it describes are all standards of the voluntary licensing body rather than state law. Curriculum, texts, calendar, testing, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 4. Tier B: the instruments were not opened.

portability.instrument: Haw. Const. art. X, § 1
portability.note: The constitution bars the appropriation of public funds for the support or benefit of any sectarian or nonsectarian private educational institution, subject only to a special purpose revenue bond exception added in 1994 and extended in 2002 that finances facilities rather than tuition. No voucher, account, scholarship, or tax credit program for private school attendance is in force, and Hawaii is recorded as having declined the federal tax credit election. The anchor for no program.

household.note: Notice of intent goes to the local public school principal, the parent keeps a record of the planned curriculum, test scores are required at grades three, five, eight, and ten, and an annual progress report goes to the principal. The principal reviews the adequacy of the child's progress, may require the curriculum record, and on inadequate progress over two consecutive semesters may recommend enrollment in a school or action for educational neglect. Review by a state official is the anchor for 1, and section 8-12-20 grants no course credits for time spent home-schooled, which restricts hybrid arrangements as well.

security.instrument: Haw. Const. art. X, § 1
security.note: A restrictive constitutional provision is in force, renumbered from article IX by the 1978 convention and amended twice since only to widen a revenue bond exception, which is the anchor for 1. Nothing is pending on the register, which is why it is not lower.

formation.note: Section 33-202 discharges the compulsory attendance duty by enrollment in a private or parochial school and attaches no registration, approval, or licensure to operating one; accreditation under section 33-119 is optional. No filing at all is required of the school, which is the anchor for 4.

autonomy.note: Section 33-202 requires instruction in the subjects commonly and usually taught in the public schools and a session equal in length to the public schools, and nothing further: no state assessment is mandated, and the certification duty in section 33-1201 reaches only accredited private schools, which accreditation is itself optional. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3; the calendar requirement is why 4 is not taken.

portability.instrument: Idaho Code § 63-3029N (2025 Idaho Sess. Laws ch. 9, § 2)
portability.note: A refundable credit of up to $5,000 per student, $7,500 for a student with a disability, is open to every Idaho resident aged five to eighteen with no eligibility ceiling, nonpublic school tuition is a qualified expense, and the section provides that a school may not be required to alter its creed, practices, admissions policy, or curriculum to enroll a credit-funded student. A universal program open to religious schools with no condition reaching religious character is the anchor for 4; the $50,000,000 annual ceiling and the priority given to families under 300 percent of the federal poverty level are rationing devices, not eligibility limits.

household.note: The section requires only that a parent cause the child to be instructed in the subjects commonly and usually taught in the public schools. No notice, registration, assessment, or portfolio is required of a home-educating family, which is the anchor for 4.

security.instrument: Idaho Const. art. IX, § 5
security.note: Article IX, section 5 forbids the legislature or any public corporation ever to make an appropriation or pay from any public fund anything in aid of any church or sectarian or religious society. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1 whatever the statutory position, and the 2025 credit has not been tested against it.

formation.note: Section 26-1 exempts a child attending a private or parochial school teaching the branches of education taught in the public schools and conditions that exemption on nothing else: registration with the State Board and the recognition process that follows it are both elective. No required filing to operate is the anchor for 4.

autonomy.note: The statute prescribes the branches of education taught at the corresponding age and grade in the public schools and instruction in English, and no more; no state assessment is mandated and educator licensure is not required. The instructional day, degree, and evaluation rules in Part 425 bind only a school that has elected recognition. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing the school's own is the anchor for 3.

portability.instrument: 35 ILCS 5/201(m); Griffith v. Bower, 319 Ill. App. 3d 993 (5th Dist. 2001)
portability.note: The one program still in force is a credit of 25 percent of qualified education expenses above $250, capped at $500 for the family, for tuition, book fees, and lab fees at a public or nonpublic school, and the court records that religious schools are eligible. A capped tax credit is the anchor for 2; the credit has also been income-limited since 2018.

household.note: Home education proceeds under the private school exemption in section 26-1, which imposes no notice, registration, or assessment; notification of the State Board is voluntary. No notice and no assessment required is the anchor for 4. A regional superintendent may ask a family to establish that instruction is commensurate with the public schools, but that is a burden on challenge rather than a standing requirement.

security.instrument: 35 ILCS 40/65 (Invest in Kids Act, repealed 1 January 2025); Ill. Const. art. X, § 3
security.note: The Invest in Kids scholarship tax credit expired after tax year 2023 and the Act repealed itself on 1 January 2025, with no extending legislation located; article X, section 3 also stands. A protection repealed within the last two years is the anchor for 0. The constitutional provision was opened; the repealing section of the Act was not, and the repeal rests on the compiled index.

formation.note: A nonpublic school that is neither accredited nor state board approved may operate without registration, approval, or licensure, and its only dealing with the state is to furnish the number of students by grade level on the request of the secretary of education. Notification at the state's option and nothing more is the anchor for 4; accreditation and recognition are both elective.

autonomy.note: The section provides that such a school 'is not bound by any requirements set forth in IC 20 or IC 21 with regard to curriculum or the content of educational programs offered by the school.' Personnel licensure and ISTEP participation attach only to accredited or recognized schools. Curriculum, texts, staffing, and testing all the school's own is the anchor for 4.

portability.note: As the definition now stands an eligible choice scholarship student is any individual with legal settlement in Indiana who is at least five and less than twenty-two years of age on 1 October, with no household income limit, and section 20-51-4-2 entitles that student to a scholarship at an eligible school. A universal program open to religious schools is the anchor for 4.

household.note: Home instruction is carried on as a nonaccredited nonpublic school, exempt from curriculum requirements, reporting enrollment only on the secretary's request and keeping attendance records producible on request. No standing notice and no assessment is the anchor for 4; the 180-day instruction duty is a duty on the parent and not a filing.

security.instrument: Meredith v. Pence, 984 N.E.2d 1213 (Ind. 2013); Ind. Const. art. 1, §§ 4, 6
security.note: The Indiana Supreme Court upheld the Choice Scholarship Program against article 8, section 1 and against both religion clauses, holding that the benefit runs to families through private choice and that section 6 was not aimed at primary and secondary schools. Nothing is pending, which is the anchor for 3; 4 is not taken because the program was materially amended as recently as 2025 and the settled position is a judicial construction of provisions that remain restrictive on their face.

formation.instrument: Iowa Code § 256.11; Iowa Admin. Code r. 281-12.10
formation.note: A nonpublic school is held to the education standards through accreditation, and the rule provides that a school may be accredited by an approved independent accrediting agency instead of by the state board, with the Association of Christian Schools International, Christian Schools International, and National Lutheran School Accreditation on the approved list. Accreditation required, satisfied by a religious accreditor the state recognizes, is the anchor for 2.

autonomy.instrument: Iowa Code § 256.11(5); Iowa Admin. Code r. 281-12.4(8)
autonomy.note: Section 256.11 prescribes a detailed minimum educational program and named graduation units for accredited nonpublic schools, and rule 281-12.4(8) requires teachers in state board accredited nonpublic schools to hold a license for the position held. Teacher credentials required, with the religious content of instruction not reached, is the anchor for 2. Section 256.11(16) softens this for schools using an independent accreditor, which is why this sits at 2 rather than 1.

portability.instrument: Iowa Code § 257.11B(2)(a)(3) (2023 Iowa Acts ch. 1, Students First Act)
portability.note: The eligibility phase-in ended: for school budget years beginning on or after July 1, 2025 all resident pupils eligible to enroll in kindergarten through grade twelve who will attend a nonpublic school are eligible for an education savings account payment. Universal eligibility in force is the anchor for 4.

household.note: Independent private instruction requires no filing at all and is 'exempt from all state statutes and administrative rules applicable to a school,' and section 299A.3 says a parent providing competent private instruction 'may' report and have the child evaluated, which makes reporting and assessment optional rather than required. No notice and no assessment is the anchor for 4. The independent private instruction conditions do cap a paid hybrid at four unrelated students and no tuition, which is the one respect in which Iowa falls short of the anchor.

security.instrument: Iowa Const. art. I, § 3; Iowa Code § 257.11B
security.note: Iowa's provision is a compelled support clause and not a general bar on aid to sectarian schools, so no restrictive constitutional provision is in force, and no litigation against the education savings account program is on the register. Statutory with nothing pending is the anchor for 3; it is not 4 because the position rests on a statute enacted in 2023 rather than on anything constitutional or long settled.

formation.note: Attendance at a private, denominational, or parochial school taught by a competent instructor for substantially the public school period satisfies the compulsory attendance law, with no approval or accreditation required, and the school's only duty is to register its name and address with the State Board. Ministerial registration that the state records is the anchor for 3. Section 72-3120 was opened; the registration sections were not, and rest on the federal compilation. The approval requirement in that statute applies only to an alternative program a church offers to students who have completed the eighth grade, and is not a condition on religious schools generally.

autonomy.note: For a school that has not elected state accreditation the statute requires a competent instructor and a period of instruction substantially equivalent to the public schools, and prescribes no subjects, texts, credentials, or assessments; the curriculum and testing duties in K.S.A. 72-1101 et seq. and K.A.R. 91-31-32 follow accreditation, which is voluntary. The instructional-hours floor is why 4 is not taken; on the anchors this sits at 3.

portability.instrument: K.S.A. 72-4352; K.S.A. 72-4357 (Tax Credit for Low Income Students Scholarship Program)
portability.note: The single program is a scholarship funded by contributions carrying a 75 percent income tax credit, open only to a child whose annual family income is at or below 250 percent of the federal poverty guidelines and who satisfies a prior public school attendance condition, with the credits capped at $10,000,000 a year. A narrow, income- and category-limited scholarship is the anchor for 2.

household.note: Kansas has no separate home school statute; a home school registers its name and address as a nonaccredited private school and instructs through a competent instructor for substantially equivalent hours. Notice with no assessment or review is the anchor for 3. The registration section and the Sawyer decision, which treats periodic testing as one factor a court may weigh, were not opened.

security.instrument: Kan. Const. art. 6, § 6(c)
security.note: Article 6, section 6(c) provides that no religious sect or sects shall control any part of the public educational funds. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1, and the scholarship program's tax credit structure has not been tested against it.

formation.instrument: KRS 159.030(1)(b); Kentucky State Bd. for Elementary & Secondary Educ. v. Rudasill, 589 S.W.2d 877 (Ky. 1979)
formation.note: A child enrolled in a private, parochial, or church regular day school is exempt from compulsory attendance, and the school's only duty is to notify the local board of the students in attendance. No approval, licensure, or accreditation is required, and Rudasill holds that the state may not apply its accreditation standards to such schools. Ministerial reporting that the state records is the anchor for 3.

autonomy.instrument: KRS 158.080; Kentucky State Bd. for Elementary & Secondary Educ. v. Rudasill, 589 S.W.2d 877 (Ky. 1979)
autonomy.note: Instruction must be in English and in the branches of study required in the public schools, but Rudasill held under section 5 of the Kentucky Constitution that the state may not require certified teachers or approved textbooks in private and church schools, and no state assessment is mandated. Broad subject areas prescribed with texts and staffing the school's own is the anchor for 3.

portability.note: Section 189 forbids any fund raised for educational purposes to be appropriated to or used in aid of any church, sectarian, or denominational school. No program is in force: the Education Opportunity Account Act was held to violate section 184 in December 2022, and the constitutional amendment that would have permitted such support was rejected by the voters on 5 November 2024. The anchor for no program.

household.note: A home school is treated as a private school and notifies the local board of the names, ages, and residences of its pupils within two weeks of the start of the school year. No assessment or portfolio review is required, which is the anchor for 3.

security.note: Two restrictive provisions are in force, section 189 unamended since 1891, and the attempt to displace them by constitutional amendment failed at the polls in November 2024. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1.

formation.note: A nonpublic school may either seek approval from the Board of Elementary and Secondary Education or operate without it by filing an annual enrollment registration, and the department states that collecting that information 'does not serve as approval.' Annual reporting that the state records rather than evaluates is the anchor for 3. Section 17:236 was opened; the registration alternative rests on the department's page.

autonomy.note: The statute requires a minimum of 180 days of operation, and it confines the certification duty to schools receiving state or federal funds: a school receiving no public funds may employ instructors meeting requirements 'as may be prescribed by the school or the church.' State assessment participation is optional. The 180-day floor is why 4 is not taken; on the anchors this sits at 3. The certification condition attaches to public money and is scored under portability, not here.

portability.instrument: Act No. 1 of the 2024 Regular Session (SB 313), LA GATOR Scholarship Program
portability.note: Education scholarship accounts may be spent on nonpublic school tuition and fees, tutoring, therapies, textbooks, and dual enrollment, and the department reports about 6,000 students funded from a $43,500,000 appropriation for 2025-2026 under a three-phase eligibility rollout that gives priority to former Louisiana Scholarship Program students and to lower-income families. A broad program in force but still category-limited in its current phase is the anchor for 3. The enacting act was not opened.

household.note: A home study program must be approved by the Board of Elementary and Secondary Education on an application filed within fifteen days of commencement, and renewal by 1 October requires satisfactory evidence of a sustained curriculum of quality at least equal to the public schools, shown by a documentation packet, standardized test scores, or a certified teacher's attestation. Approval of a plan is the anchor for 1. A family may instead register as a nonpublic school not seeking state approval, but the department states that registration does not confirm compliance with compulsory attendance and the resulting diploma is not equivalent.

security.instrument: La. Const. art. VIII, § 13(B); Louisiana Federation of Teachers v. State, 118 So. 3d 1033 (La. 2013)
security.note: Section 13(B) requires the minimum foundation program formula to allocate funds to parish and city school systems, and in 2013 the Supreme Court struck down the diversion of those funds to nonpublic entities. Louisiana has no bar on aid to religious schools as such, so the position is statutory, but the funding route is constrained and the current program is new, appropriation-funded, and mid-rollout. Statutory with live movement in either direction is the anchor for 2.

formation.note: Attendance satisfies compulsory attendance only at a private school approved for attendance purposes or recognized by the department as providing equivalent instruction, and section 2901 gives a school two routes: accreditation by a New England association of schools and colleges, or compliance with the department's section 2902 requirements. Approval is required and the only accreditor route is a secular regional association, which is the anchor for 1.

autonomy.note: An approved private school must provide instruction in the basic curriculum established by rule by the commissioner and in alignment with the system of learning results, and must 'employ only certified teachers.' Teacher credentials required, with the religious content of instruction not itself prescribed, is the anchor for 2. A school approved for tuition purposes carries a heavier load under section 2951(6) and the Maine Human Rights Act, but that overlay attaches only to schools that take public money.

portability.instrument: 20-A M.R.S. § 2951(6); 5 M.R.S. § 4602; St. Dominic Academy v. Makin, No. 24-1739 (1st Cir. July 2, 2026)
portability.note: Town tuitioning is in statute and the nonsectarian condition at section 2951(2) was repealed by PL 2025, c. 112, but approval for tuition purposes still carries the statewide assessment and learning results conditions of section 2951(6) and the Maine Human Rights Act rules of 5 M.R.S. § 4602, and the First Circuit held on July 2, 2026 that the religious expression rule burdens religious exercise and is not neutral. A program in force carrying conditions that reach religious character is the anchor for 1.

household.note: Written notice of intent goes to the administrative unit and the commissioner within 10 days and an annual letter follows each September 1 enclosing one of five forms of assessment. Two of the five, review by any individual holding a current Maine teacher's certificate and portfolio review by a local homeschooling support group, are the family's own choice. Notice plus assessment with the reviewer of the family's choosing is the anchor for 2.

security.instrument: St. Dominic Academy v. Makin, No. 24-1739 (1st Cir. July 2, 2026); Crosspoint Church v. Makin, No. 24-1590 (1st Cir. July 2, 2026)
security.note: Maine has no restrictive constitutional provision on aid to religious schools, and the position is moving in both directions at once: the sectarian exclusion was repealed in 2025 while two First Circuit appeals decided on July 2, 2026 remain on remand. Statutory with active litigation that could move the position either way is the anchor for 2; not 1, because the live cases would add a protection rather than remove one.

formation.note: A noncollegiate educational institution may not operate without a certificate of approval from the State Board, but the subsection 'does not apply to an institution operated by a bona fide church organization,' which registers its operation instead. For a church-operated Christian school the requirement is a recorded registration, which is the anchor for 3; a private school outside the church exemption faces approval and would sit lower.

autonomy.note: The department states that a church-exempt school is outside COMAR 13A.09.09 altogether and so is subject to no state curriculum standard, teacher qualification, or testing mandate, and 'operates its educational program in accordance with standards that are established by the governing church'; only zoning, health, fire, background check, and reporting rules apply. Curriculum, texts, calendar, testing, and staffing all the school's own is the anchor for 4. The exemption statute was opened; the scope of the regulation rests on the department's fact sheet.

portability.instrument: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Program, created 2016 by annual budget appropriation
portability.note: The one program is a scholarship funded through the annual budget bill rather than a permanent authorizing statute, limited to families at or below the free and reduced-price meal income limit. A narrow, income-limited scholarship is the anchor for 2. Recorded from a dated national inventory; no enacting instrument exists to open, the appropriation language itself was not located.

household.note: A family notifies the local superintendent and then chooses its supervisor: under the local school system the representative may review a portfolio of materials not more than three times a year, while a family supervised by a church-exempt school or a church education ministry is outside the portfolio review entirely. Notice plus a review by a reviewer of the family's choosing is the anchor for 2.

security.instrument: BOOST Program (annual budget appropriation); Bethel Ministries, Inc. v. Salmon, D. Md. (2021)
security.note: Maryland has no restrictive constitutional provision reaching aid to religious schools, but the program rests on an annual appropriation and can lapse in any session, and a federal court has already had to order a Christian school back into it after the administering board excluded the school on viewpoint grounds. Statutory and live in either direction is the anchor for 2. Recorded from a dated national inventory; the opinion was not opened.

formation.note: Attendance at a private school satisfies the compulsory attendance law only where the school committee has approved it, being 'satisfied that the instruction in all the studies required by law equals in thoroughness and efficiency, and in the progress made therein, that in the public schools in the same town.' Approval is required and only the designated public body can give it, which is the anchor for 1; 0 is not taken because the same sentence provides that committees 'shall not withhold such approval on account of religious teaching.'

autonomy.instrument: Mass. Gen. Laws c. 76, § 1; Mass. Gen. Laws c. 72, § 2
autonomy.note: The studies required by law are prescribed and the local committee judges thoroughness and efficiency, but no state assessment is mandated, no teacher certification is required, and religious teaching is expressly excluded as a ground of decision; enrollment and withdrawal reports under chapter 72 are clerical. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing the school's own is the anchor for 3, with the committee's discretion under the thoroughness standard noted as the reason a later coder might argue 2.

portability.instrument: Mass. Const. Amend. art. XVIII, § 2 (as amended by arts. XLVI and CIII)
portability.note: The anti-aid amendment bars any grant, appropriation, or use of public money for founding, maintaining, or aiding any primary or secondary school 'which is not publicly owned and under the exclusive control, order and supervision of public officers,' and reserves its exception to higher education. No program is in force. The anchor for no program.

household.instrument: Mass. Gen. Laws c. 76, § 1; Care and Protection of Charles, 399 Mass. 324 (1987)
household.note: The statute excuses a child 'being otherwise instructed in a manner approved in advance by the superintendent or the school committee,' and the reviewing authority may require periodic standardized testing or other evaluation. Advance approval of the family's plan by a public official is the anchor for 1.

security.instrument: Mass. Const. Amend. art. XVIII, § 2 (as amended by arts. XLVI and CIII)
security.note: A restrictive constitutional provision, adopted in 1917 and tightened in 1974, is in force and was applied by the Supreme Judicial Court as recently as 2018. That is the anchor for 1 whatever the statutory position.

formation.note: A nonpublic school satisfying compulsory attendance must be approved by the state, and a boarding school must be accredited by a national association the state department recognizes. Approval is required and the recognized accreditor is not the school's free choice, which is the anchor for 1 rather than 2.

autonomy.instrument: MCL 380.1561(3)(a); MCL 380.1166; MCL 388.553; People v. DeJonge, 442 Mich. 266
autonomy.note: Subjects must be comparable to the local public schools and named courses are required, but content, texts, and staffing are the school's own; teacher certification is optional and religious objection waives the minimum, and state assessment is optional. Broad subject areas prescribed, content free: the anchor for 3.

portability.instrument: Mich. Const. art. VIII, sec. 2
portability.note: Michigan's constitution forbids public support of nonpublic schools, and no program is in force. Scored 0 on the anchor for no program.

household.note: Reporting to the department is voluntary unless special education services are sought, and no assessment is required. The anchor for 4.

security.instrument: Mich. Const. art. VIII, sec. 2
security.note: A restrictive constitutional provision is in force, which is the anchor for 1 whatever the statutory position.

formation.note: No registration, approval, or licensure conditions the operation of a nonpublic school, and accreditation is optional, but the school reports the name, birth date, and address of each child, the tests intended to be used, the name of each instructor, and evidence of compliance to the local superintendent by 1 October each year. Annual reporting that is recorded rather than evaluated is the anchor for 3.

autonomy.note: Subject areas are prescribed, every instructor must satisfy one of five qualification criteria, and subdivision 11 requires a school that has not elected accreditation to administer a nationally norm-referenced standardized achievement examination every year. A mandated assessment and instructor credentials, with the religious content of instruction untouched, is the anchor for 2.

portability.instrument: Minn. Stat. § 290.0132, subd. 4; Minn. Stat. § 290.0674
portability.note: The subtraction sustained in Mueller v. Allen remains, allowing $1,625 per child in kindergarten through grade 6 and $2,500 in grades 7 through 12 for tuition and fees paid to attend a school. The separate education credit is larger but does not reach tuition for regular day instruction and expressly excludes religious instruction from its qualifying fees. A narrow deduction is the anchor for 2, and the credit's religious-instruction exclusion is recorded here for a later coder.

household.note: A family files a full report by 1 October of the first year and a letter of intent to continue in each later year, and must give the child a nationally norm-referenced standardized achievement examination every year, the examination and its administration being agreed with the superintendent. Notice plus an annual assessment is the anchor for 2; 1 is not taken because no plan is approved and no state official reviews the child's work, though the examination is not purely the family's own choice.

security.instrument: Minn. Const. art. XIII, § 2
security.note: The constitution provides that in no case shall public money or property be appropriated or used for the support of schools wherein the distinctive doctrines, creeds, or tenets of any particular Christian or other religious sect are promulgated or taught. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1.

formation.instrument: Miss. Code Ann. § 37-13-91(3); Miss. Code Ann. § 37-17-7
formation.note: No registration, approval, or licensure is required to operate a nonpublic school, state accreditation and approval are both requested at the school's option, and the section states that the state has no authority to control, manage, or supervise a nonpublic school or to make any suggestion as to its control or management. The anchor for 4; the certificate of enrollment is filed for each child under the compulsory attendance law and is not a condition on the school's existence.

autonomy.note: The disclaimer of any power to control, manage, or supervise leaves curriculum, texts, calendar, and staffing to the school; no subjects are prescribed, no statewide assessment is required, and teacher certification follows only from voluntary state accreditation. The anchor for 4.

portability.instrument: Miss. Code Ann. §§ 37-181-1 to 37-181-23 (Equal Opportunity for Students with Special Needs Act)
portability.note: The education scholarship account may be spent on tuition and academic fees at an eligible school, curricula, tutoring, and therapies, but the program reaches only a student identified as having a disability under the federal statute, and it stands repealed effective 1 July 2028. A program limited to particular students is the anchor for 2; the separate dyslexia therapy scholarship is narrower still.

household.note: A parent files a certificate of enrollment giving the child's and parent's details and a description of the type of education with the local school attendance officer on or before 15 September each year, and nothing else: no assessment, no portfolio, no approval. Notice with no assessment is the anchor for 3.

security.instrument: Miss. Const. art. 8, § 208
security.note: Section 208 forbids any funds to be appropriated toward the support of any sectarian school or any school not conducted as a free school, and the Mississippi Supreme Court disposed of the 2024 challenge to a grant program for independent schools on standing without reaching that question, so the provision stands unadjudicated. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1.

formation.instrument: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 167.031; Missouri Department of Elementary and Secondary Education, Nonpublic School Registration
formation.note: Section 167.031 discharges the compulsory attendance duty by enrollment in a private, parochial, or parish school and attaches no approval, accreditation, or licensure to operating one. The federal compilation reports registration as mandatory; the department's own page records that a nonpublic school wishing to apply for federal and state grant programs may request to be added to the Nonpublic Registration system, which makes registration voluntary and a condition on money rather than on operating, so it is excluded from formation and recorded under portability. No filing is required to operate, which is the anchor for 4. Tier B because the correction rests on the department's page rather than on statutory text.

autonomy.instrument: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 167.031.3; Mo. Rev. Stat. § 170.011; Mo. Rev. Stat. § 170.345
autonomy.note: Section 167.031.3 provides that no department or agency of the state may dictate any statewide curriculum for private, parochial, or parish schools, and that such a school need not include any concept, topic, or practice in conflict with its religious doctrines. Courses in the constitutions and in American history are prescribed by section 170.011, and section 170.345 requires a student entering the ninth grade after 1 July 2017 at any public, charter, or private school to pass an examination on the provisions and principles of American civics to graduate. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3; the anchor for 2 is not taken because the civics examination is a graduation condition the school itself administers rather than a state assessment, and no teacher credential is required.

portability.note: A qualified student is a resident of the state, not an illegal alien, whose household income does not exceed 300 percent of the income standard used to qualify for free and reduced price lunches, and who attended public school full time for a semester, is eligible to begin kindergarten or first grade, or is the sibling of a prior recipient. Senate Bill 727 removed the geographic limitation and raised the program cap to $75,000,000. A broad program, income-limited, open to religious schools on the same terms as others is the anchor for 3; the prior-attendance and income conditions are why 4 is not taken.

household.instrument: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 167.031.2; Mo. Rev. Stat. § 167.042
household.note: Notice to the superintendent of schools or the recorder of county deeds is permissive and is not mandated, and the family's duties are 1,000 hours of instruction with at least 600 in the basics, at least 400 of those 600 at the home location, and a plan book, diary, daily log, or other written record. No assessment is required and no official reviews the record. The anchor for 4 is not taken because the hours and the written record are mandatory; the anchor for 3 is taken on a regime lighter in notice and heavier in recordkeeping than the anchor describes. Tier B because subsection 2 did not render in the published section and the hours provisions rest on the federal compilation.

security.instrument: Mo. Const. art. I, § 7; Mo. Const. art. IX, § 8
security.note: Article I, section 7 forbids money ever being taken from the public treasury, directly or indirectly, in aid of any church, sect, or denomination of religion, and article IX, section 8 forbids the general assembly or any local corporation ever to make an appropriation in aid of any religious creed, church, or sectarian purpose. A restrictive constitutional provision in force is the anchor for 1 whatever the statutory position, and the scholarship account program, which is funded by tax credits rather than appropriation, has not been tested against either.

formation.instrument: Mont. Code Ann. § 20-5-109; Mont. Code Ann. § 20-7-102
formation.note: Section 20-5-109 conditions the compulsory enrollment exemption on keeping attendance and immunization records available to the county superintendent on request, minimum aggregate instruction hours, a building complying with applicable local health and safety regulations, and an organized course of study, and it requires notice only of home schools. No registration, approval, or licensure of a nonpublic school is required, and accreditation under section 20-7-102 is granted on the school's own request. The anchor for 4 is taken.

autonomy.instrument: Mont. Code Ann. § 20-5-109(2), (4); Mont. Code Ann. § 20-7-111; Admin. R. Mont. 10.55.605; Admin. R. Mont. 10.56.101
autonomy.note: The school must provide the minimum aggregate hours and an organized course of study that includes the subjects required of public schools as a basic instructional program, and nothing further: content, texts, and staffing are the school's own. The educator license required by rule 10.55.605 and the state-level assessments required by rule 10.56.101 attach only to an accredited school, and accreditation is voluntary, so both are excluded. Broad subject areas prescribed with content free is the anchor for 3.

portability.instrument: Mont. Code Ann. §§ 15-30-3101 to 15-30-3114 (2015 Mont. Laws ch. 457, as amended by 2021 Mont. Laws ch. 480 and 2023 Mont. Laws ch. 558)
portability.note: The one program in force is a credit against the income tax for donations to a student scholarship organization, capped at $200,000 per donor, with scholarships limited to half of the state per-pupil spending figure. A narrow tax credit is the anchor for 2. The special needs education savings account under sections 20-7-1701 to 20-7-1710 is not counted toward the score: it was held unconstitutional in December 2025 and is on appeal, which is recorded under security. The condition that a participating school be accredited or in the process of accreditation is a condition on the money and is excluded from formation.

household.instrument: Mont. Code Ann. § 20-5-109(5); Mont. Code Ann. § 20-5-111
household.note: A home school must notify the county superintendent of the student's attendance in each school fiscal year, and section 20-5-111 makes the parent solely responsible for the educational philosophy, the selection of instructional materials, curriculum, and textbooks, the time, place, and method of instruction, and the evaluation of the instruction. Notice required with no assessment and no portfolio review is the anchor for 3.

security.instrument: Montana Quality Education Coalition v. State, No. ADV-2024-44 (Mont. 1st Jud. Dist. Ct., Dec. 2025), on appeal, Mont. No. DA 26-0179; Mont. Const. art. X, § 6
security.note: The district court granted the plaintiffs summary judgment holding the special needs education savings account program unconstitutional for want of an appropriation made by law under article VIII, section 14, and stayed its judgment only until the conclusion of the 2026 school fiscal year, with the appeal docketed as DA 26-0179. A protection enjoined within the last two years is the anchor for 0, and the no-aid provision at article X, section 6 remains in force notwithstanding Espinoza v. Montana Department of Revenue, 591 U.S. 464 (2020).

formation.note: A private, denominational, or parochial school either meets the section 79-318 approval or accreditation requirements or elects not to, and the election 'shall be effective when a statement is received by the Commissioner of Education' stating that those requirements violate sincerely held religious beliefs. Rules are confined by statute to procedures for receiving that information. A filing the state records rather than evaluates is the anchor for 3.

autonomy.note: A school that elects out must maintain 'a sequential program of instruction designed to lead to basic skills in the language arts, mathematics, science, social studies, and health,' and individuals it employs 'shall not be required to meet the certification requirements' of sections 79-801 to 79-815. No state assessment is imposed on such a school. Broad subject areas prescribed with content, texts, and staffing left to the school is the anchor for 3.

portability.instrument: Neb. Const. art. VII, § 11; LB 1402 (2024), §§ 5 and 7; Referendum Measure 435 (Nov. 5, 2024)
portability.note: LB 1402 repealed the 2023 Opportunity Scholarships Act outright, and the voters then repealed section 1 of LB 1402 at the general election of November 5, 2024 by 508,140 to 382,921. Nothing is left in force and the constitution bars appropriations to schools not owned or exclusively controlled by the state. The anchor for no program.

household.note: An annual statement of election and assurances is filed with the Commissioner, stating the ground of the election, that basic instruction in the five named subjects will be provided, and that the individuals monitoring instruction are qualified. The statute requires no assessment and no portfolio review, which is the anchor for 3. Recorded caveat: the federal compilation describes a curriculum scope-and-sequence submission and departmental achievement testing under 92 NAC 12, sections 004 and 008, which I did not verify against the rule text; if those survive in the current rule the component would fall to 2 or 1.
